statusText: Mapped policy state: WATCH. Nasdaq-100 is grinding at session highs in an orderly, low-volatility advance; Tail remains below the block threshold.
recommendation: Mapped policy state: WATCH for both NQ futures and NAS100 CFD. Observed one-way drift from the session low to the session high argues against treating intraday dips as fully reliable mean-reversion points, while VIX near 14.3 and a 0.7% session range keep Tail well under the blocking band. The narrow evidence-based danger window covers the 19:00-20:15Z power hour and cash close, where late-session continuation is the nearest amplifier. Existing-position management and emergency protection remain active throughout.
headline: NDX at session highs on AI and falling oil; orderly trend keeps Tail in the watch band
body: At the assessment cutoff the Nasdaq-100 is near 30,708, up about 0.74%, trading within a few points of its 30,711.94 session high after opening at the 30,496.43 session low. That open-to-high path is genuine directional efficiency and the clearest current Tail input, but its amplitude is small: the session range is roughly 0.7% and VIX is near 14.3, down about 3.8% and sitting close to its own daily low. Cross-asset inputs are supportive rather than discontinuous. WTI is near $90 (-2.2%) and Brent near $99 (-1.3%), extending a fifth straight session of declines on reports that Iran may reopen the Strait of Hormuz within seven days; that is a de-escalating geopolitical input, which lowers rather than raises path risk. The 10-year note yield is near 4.95%, marginally lower on the day after slipping back below 5%, and the 2-year auction stopped at 4.787%, both consistent with the quarter-point Federal Reserve rate increase delivered last week. Breadth conflicts with the index move: the Dow is down about 0.4% while the Nasdaq-100 is up 0.74%, so leadership is narrow and megacap- and semiconductor-driven, following Meta's Muse AI app reaching the top of the App Store and last session's chip rally. Conflicting breadth of this kind reduces directional conviction and lifts Stress more than it lifts Tail. Offsetting the calm tape, Richmond Fed President Barkin said supply shocks are not proving short-lived and left the door open to further rate increases, and the Richmond Fed manufacturing index printed -2 against a forecast of 3. The combination of a hiking central bank, a 10-year near 5% and record index levels is a genuinely two-sided, higher-stress backdrop, but the observed price path today is an orderly low-volatility grind rather than a violent no-retracement repricing. Tail is therefore set at 20, reflecting session-extreme holding and observed directional efficiency, while remaining far below the blocking band. The next scheduled catalysts are the US power hour and 20:00Z cash close today, then the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z on 23 September, fifteen minutes after the cash open.

lookbackSummary: The previous 24 published hours cover a full cycle. The 21 September US afternoon carried elevated Tail of 32-33 with a trend-up mode, which unwound sharply into that cash close as Tail fell to 23 and then 14. The overnight and European hours of 22 September were consistently quiet, with Tail between 11 and 13 and a normal mode for thirteen straight hours. Tail lifted to 21 at the 22 September cash open, then eased back to 17, 15 and 14 through the US morning as the mode was assessed as mixed and no persistent one-way structure developed.
outlookSummary: The near-term path is shaped by the US power hour and the 20:00Z cash close, where late-session continuation of the observed open-to-high drift is the nearest conditional amplifier and Tail is carried at 21-22. Conditional Tail then decays through the post-close and overnight hours to 12-13 as cash liquidity leaves and no scheduled catalyst is in force, with mean reversion the base case across the Asian session. Risk rebuilds gradually through the European morning to 14-15, conditional on yields, since the 10-year near 4.95% and last week's rate increase leave the rate-sensitive megacap leadership exposed. The clear peak of the forecast is the 13:00Z window on 23 September, where the US cash open at 13:30Z overlaps the S&P Global flash PMIs at 13:45Z; that slot is carried at Tail 22 in an event/whipsaw mode as a two-way catalyst checkpoint, not as an assumed directional break. Conditional Tail then eases to 18-19 through the following US session, with the 5-year note auction at 17:00Z a further yield checkpoint. No forecast hour reaches the blocking band.
